Sam

Sam —

Appreciate the model, good detail. Internal owners looped in. Quick notes:
- We're happy to provision a time-bounded quota bump for the pilot day, but we need to lock down exact routes and model variants (full-gen vs. condensed) by EOD Monday so we can pre-warm KV caches and set batching profiles.
- Can you highlight which endpoints are latency-sensitive (cart-checkout vs. product-summary) and the % of requests that can accept a 300–500ms added tail? That will determine fallback mapping.
- We typically require a one-page addendum for a temporary quota uplift + a billing estimate. I'll spin up an ops playbook template and ask Product/Runtime to answer two clarifying product questions below.

Product asks (Irene + Priyom, see inline):
1) For long-lived sessions (30s+ token generation with streaming), do we have a recommended KV cache TTL override for pilot traffic to avoid cold-KV churn?
2) Does runtime support per-route transient quantization profiles (e.g., 8-bit for non-sensitive summarization routes) without a model load delay that would break the pre-warm?

Ops asks (Priyom / Connor):
- Preferred uplift window length (we propose 6 hours centered on peak) and exact burst headroom % (we can be conservative and add a 25% buffer).
- Contact list for SRE on-call (name/phone/pager) for D-day escalation.

I'll draft the addendum and estimated spend once we get route mappings. Can we have a short internal sync at 10:30 PST Mon to lock routes?

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PeakRetail BF pilot - provisional throughput ask and traffic model

Thanks Markus / Sam (looping since Sam is external). Short answers to the product asks:

1) KV cache TTL: for pilot traffic we recommend extending session-KV TTL to 12 minutes (default 2m) for streaming sessions longer than 20s. That reduces KV cold-starts and keeps memory usage predictable. We'll tag the feature as a transient policy scoped to the customer ID so it does not affect global cache LRU.

2) Transient quantization profiles: runtime supports switching to quantized execution per route but requires loading a compatible kernel set. If the quantized variant is already warmed on the node pool, switching is near-instant; if not, a first-request load time can be 8–12s. For this pilot I recommend pre-warming quantized variants for low-sensitivity routes during the pre-warm window.

Product questions for Sam: can you flag which routes are candidates for 8-bit profiles (list by route path) and which must remain full-precision? That lets us provision both kernel sets ahead of D-day.

Irene Choi
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Team —

From an ops perspective, here's a conservative plan we can commit to with caveats:
- Proposed uplift: +30% baseline throughput for a 6-hour window with a 25% emergency headroom. We'll implement an automated throttle cutover at 20% sustained error rate or 95th percentile latency > 1.2s.
- Pre-warm window: 4 hours prior to start to populate KV and quantized kernels. We need route list and sample payloads by Tue EOD to perform realistic warmup.
- Rollback policy: automatic fallback to a lighter model variant if token loss vs cost crosses threshold; manual escalation if fallback fails.

SRE contacts for on-call escalation (D-day):

Priyom Das — priyom.das@redwood.com — +1-415-555-0127

Summarizing next steps and asks so we have a single action list:
1) PeakRetail: identify endpoint routing table (paths) and mark which routes can use 8-bit quantized profiles vs which require full precision — due Tue EOD (12/22).
2) PeakRetail: provide representative payloads for warmup (sample requests) and confirm the exact 4-hour peak window and time zone for scheduling — due Tue EOD (12/22).
3) Redwood (Markus/Irene/Priyom): produce one-page temporary quota addendum and a billing estimate for +30% throughput with 25% headroom — draft by Wed 12/24.
4) Redwood Ops: schedule a 4-hour pre-warm starting 4 hours before the peak, pre-warm quantized kernels for routes flagged by PeakRetail.
5) SRE Contacts confirmed in email above; we will add on-call pager to the playbook and share a run-of-show.

I'll create a shared folder with the finalized playbook and the signed addendum link once we have confirmations. Thanks all — pushing to get this locked so PeakRetail's pilot feels resilient.

Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
